title: The Starfall Observatory
description: An atmospheric mystery adventure. Find the missing astronomer, awaken an ancient instrument, and discover what has been waiting beyond the stars.

text: The road ends in Gloam Village, a place that seems to have forgotten how to be awake. Every window is dark, though a thin blue glow hangs over the mountain to the north.
At the center of the square stands a bronze bell on a crooked wooden frame. Its surface is covered in tiny stars. A weather-beaten sign reads: THE OBSERVATORY IS CLOSED. DO NOT ANSWER THE LIGHT.

success.message: A narrow mountain path climbs behind the square. The blue glow grows brighter as you ascend.

text: The old quay stretches over a black, perfectly still lake. No boats remain, but their ropes are still tied to the posts.
Something pale is wedged between two boards near the waterline.
The village chapel is small and cold. Its stained-glass window depicts a night sky with one star missing.
A wooden offering box sits beneath the window. Someone has scratched a message into its lid: 'The key was never meant to open a door.'
The inn smells of dust and extinguished fires. A guestbook lies open on the counter.
The final entry is dated exactly one hundred years ago: 'Professor Vale says the machine has begun to answer. We leave at first light.'
You arrive at a glasshouse built into the mountainside. Most of its panes are cracked, but moonlight gathers inside as if the building were full of water.
Three enormous flowers face a brass mirror mounted on the far wall. Their petals are closed.

success.message: A service stair descends beneath the glasshouse. Warm air rises from the darkness.
The three flowers open at once. A hidden bridge unfolds from the mountainside, leading to the observatory.

failure.message: Beyond the glass, a bridge mechanism lies dormant. The flowers seem to be waiting for three separate signals, and a key-shaped hollow glints in the control plate.

text: This narrow potting room is lined with shelves of labeled jars. Most contain only dust.
One label has been written in a hurried hand: 'The flowers follow the light. Turn the mirror until the beam touches the western bloom.'
A shallow cistern occupies the center of this room. The water reflects a sky that is not visible through the ceiling.
A stone basin bears three words: LISTEN. REFLECT. REMEMBER.
Pipes and narrow walkways fill the chamber beneath the glasshouse. A huge flywheel stands motionless beside a wall of copper tubing.
A small plaque reads: 'The observatory does not run on steam. It runs on time.'
The lower chamber is lined with clock faces, all stopped at different minutes. In the center is a narrow pedestal with a shallow circular groove.
A note is pinned beneath the glass: 'One turn is enough. Do not try to make yesterday happen again.'
A maintenance alcove is almost entirely swallowed by roots. A toolbox lies open, its contents carefully arranged.
Someone has placed a small wooden bird on top of the tools.
The observatory doors open without a sound. Dust hangs in the air, illuminated by a slow pulse of blue light from somewhere above.
A portrait shows Professor Elian Vale standing beside a telescope. The painted professor has the same tired eyes as the figure visible in the glass behind you.
A spiral staircase leads to a circular gallery. The ceiling is painted with constellations, but several stars have been carefully scratched away.
A brass plaque names the missing constellations: The Lantern, The Key, and The Sleeper.
This is the archive. Shelves of journals surround a desk, where a lamp still burns with a cold blue flame.
A journal lies open to its final page. The handwriting is steady at first, then increasingly faint.
The map room contains a huge model of the night sky. Tiny brass planets hang from wires, slowly circling a dark glass sphere.
A small inscription around the sphere reads: 'The door opens inward. The answer is not above you, but within the light.'
The telescope chamber is vast. Its great instrument points through a slit in the roof toward a patch of sky where no stars shine.
A figure stands at the eyepiece, perfectly still. It is Professor Vale, unchanged from the portrait downstairs.
The professor turns. 'You brought the village's light back,' he says. 'I had begun to think the world had stopped looking.'
'I held this moment for a century because I was afraid of what came after it. But the bell sounded, and the world answered. Tell them the sky is still there. They only need to look up.'
The telescope shifts. Beyond its lens, one by one, the stars return.

inspect.name: Inspect
inspect.message: Tiny constellations are engraved around its rim. Three are missing: a lantern, a key, and a sleeping figure.

ring.name: Ring the bell
ring.message: The bell gives a deep, clear note. Far above, something answers with a brief flash of blue light.

read.name: Read notices
read.message: A faded notice says: 'If the mountain light goes dark, ring the village bell. The glasshouse will know what to do.'

brass_compass.name: Brass Compass
brass_compass.description: Its needle points toward the mountain, even when turned upside down.

star_key.name: Star Key
star_key.description: A dark brass key with a star-shaped bow. It feels faintly warm.

chapel_candle.name: Chapel Candle
chapel_candle.description: A stub of white wax. It has never been lit.

guestbook_page.name: Guestbook Page
guestbook_page.description: A page bearing the final entry from the old inn. The date is one hundred years ago.

inspect.name: Inspect
inspect.message: The mirror is clouded, but its frame can turn. A small marker points toward the western flower.

align.name: Align the mirror
align.message: You turn the mirror until a narrow beam of moonlight strikes the western flower. The three blooms shiver, then open. A low chime travels through the glasshouse.

dry_seed_pod.name: Dry Seed Pod
dry_seed_pod.description: A seed pod filled with tiny silver seeds. They rattle like distant rain.

mirror_instructions.name: Mirror Instructions
mirror_instructions.description: A handwritten instruction: turn the mirror until the beam touches the western bloom.

silver_prism.name: Silver Prism
silver_prism.description: A small prism that divides light into thin ribbons of color.

cistern_coin.name: Cistern Coin
cistern_coin.description: A coin bearing the same three constellations as the village bell.

inspect.name: Inspect
inspect.message: The wheel is heavy, but its central axle is intact. A little oil would help, though the mechanism still seems capable of moving.

turn.name: Turn the flywheel
turn.message: The wheel resists, then moves with a deep metallic groan. Pipes shudder overhead. Somewhere in the mountain, a clock begins ticking.

oil_can.name: Oil Can
oil_can.description: A small can of machine oil. It is nearly empty.

clockwork_note.name: Clockwork Note
clockwork_note.description: One turn is enough. Do not try to make yesterday happen again.

minute_hand.name: Minute Hand
minute_hand.description: A long brass hand from a clock face. Its tip is shaped like an arrow.

wooden_bird.name: Wooden Bird
wooden_bird.description: A little carved bird with one wing painted blue.

gear_fragment.name: Gear Fragment
gear_fragment.description: A broken gear tooth, worn smooth by years of use.

entry_portrait.name: Portrait of Professor Vale
entry_portrait.description: The professor looks exactly as he did one hundred years ago.

visitor_register.name: Visitor Register
visitor_register.description: The last visitor signed in one hundred years ago. The name is Elian Vale.

star_chart.name: Missing Constellations Chart
star_chart.description: A chart showing three missing constellations: The Lantern, The Key, and The Sleeper.

vale_journal.name: Professor Vale's Journal
vale_journal.description: The final pages describe a machine that can hold a single moment in place. Vale feared that if he completed the alignment, the observatory would preserve him while the rest of the world moved on.

read.name: Read the inscription
read.message: The lamp's base bears a final note: 'I did not vanish. I chose the stillness. If the bell sounds again, perhaps I can choose differently.'

orrery_model.name: Orrery Model
orrery_model.description: The tiny planets move in a pattern that matches the rhythm of the bell.

glass_star.name: Glass Star
glass_star.description: A fragile star-shaped piece of blue glass. It glows faintly in your palm.
